🗣️ Everyone saw the 62,000 figure. Almost nobody saw this bit.

Big Brother Watch's research found Cumbria Police arrested 25.7 people per 10,000 for online communications offences over five years — about two and a half times the national average.

Neighbouring Northumbria? 1.9 per 10,000. 📍

Same statute book. Same words typed into the same apps. Roughly THIRTEEN times the chance of a knock at the door, depending on which side of a county boundary your broadband lands on.

To be fair: arrest isn't conviction. Of those 62,000 arrests, about 18,500 were charged and 12,300 convicted — and some will have been for genuinely serious things nobody wants ignored. ⚖️

But recording differences don't turn 1.9 into 25.7. And for the ~50,000 arrested with no conviction, the process was the punishment.

Free speech isn't free if it depends on your postcode. 👇
